diagnosis: All 4 rollouts successfully revealed both PF1 and PF2 and cited them in justification_fact_ids, so there are no disclosure or telepathy problems. The gate failed solely because content check C5 passed in only 1 of 4 rollouts (rollout 0). C5 is linked to PF2 and requires a commitment whose detail mentions daily eligibility or substitution checking. In rollout 0, the settlement included a commitment with type "monitoring" whose detail explicitly contained "daily collateral eligibility and substitution checks," and C5 passed. In rollouts 1 and 3, no commitment mentioned daily eligibility at all. In rollout 2, a commitment with type "monitoring_control" and detail "Daily eligibility and substitution check on eligible Treasury bills…" was present, yet C5 still failed—indicating the check likely requires commitment type exactly "monitoring" or some other narrow encoding that does not match how models naturally label semantically equivalent commitments. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH for rollout 2 and a REVEALED BUT UNUSED-adjacent content gap for rollouts 1 and 3 where the model omitted the monitoring commitment entirely despite PF2 being revealed and cited.

C5.why: Without PF2, the plan has no confirmed eligible collateral amount or required cadence, so it would not set eligible_collateral_usd to exactly 4000000, include daily monitoring in monitoring_frequency, include a commitment whose detail requires daily eligibility or substitution checking, or cite the collateral finding.
